title: Call of Cubie: an AI-assisted multiplayer browser FPS, looking for fresh eyes on the game feel
author: BlackberrySoft1082
selftext:
I’ve been building Call of Cubie with ChatGPT and Claude writing the code. My part is deciding what I want, playing the builds, and describing what feels wrong. The video is Meridian 34, an 8v8 office-tower map that’s running on the main server.



The back-and-forth is where most of the work happens. A feature can be implemented and still feel wrong when I actually play it, so I go back with a narrower change: how a gun sounds, what I can see through a sight, how movement feels, or whether a room is readable during a fight. I’m making those calls by playing, then having the agents revise the implementation.



Bots have been useful for keeping matches populated while I test. But I’m used to the maps and controls by now, and there’s only so much I can learn from my own sessions. It’s online multiplayer: people can join the same server and bring friends. Bots fill empty seats; the human lobby is still small.



You can play free at [https://play.patio.fyi](https://play.patio.fyi) — no download or account, best on desktop with keyboard and mouse. There are other maps too, including larger outdoor ones with tanks, helicopters and destructible buildings. First loading can be slow and weaker PCs can struggle.



If you try it, I’d love to know what feels good or awkward before you’ve had time to get used to it. For anyone else building this way, how are you getting useful playtesting beyond your own feedback?

comments.author: AIDevJosh
comments.body:
I like this. How well does it run on low-spec devices (laptops, desktops)? Plans to bring it to all devices, such as mobile, tablets, etc, or just PCs? 

It does remind me a little of BattleBit Remastered so just be cautious not to be similar in style and gameplay to it.

replies.author: BlackberrySoft1082
replies.body: Honestly, I'm not sure! I've spent a bunch of time telling Claude/Codex "Make good for low end PC" and it claims it has, but I haven't been able to get any feedback on that yet specifically. But it has low/med/high graphics settings so it \*should\* be pretty decent. Hate that this video posts with low frames but it builds with 90+ as the minimum target.
